visible.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy partially fills a Schedule II prescription at the patient's request two days after the prescription was issued. Which assessment is correct?

The first pharmacy may dispense the balance on day 31 because the 30 days run from the initial partial fill.

visible.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy has a valid Klonopin prescription for 60 tablets that was issued two weeks ago. Only 20 tablets are in stock, and the patient asks to receive 20 now and the balance later. Under federal law, which approach is permissible?

Dispense 20 now; record each partial fill, keep the aggregate at 60 or less, and finish within six months of issue.
Dispense 20 now and restart the six-month dispensing window when the balance is received.
Refuse the partial fill because Schedule IV prescriptions must be dispensed in a single transaction.
Dispense the balance later without documenting each partial because the original order already states 60 tablets.

choice_analysis.A: A new prescription is not automatically required merely because a Schedule IV prescription is partially filled.

choice_analysis.C: A partial fill does not restart the six-month period; the original issue date continues to control.
choice_analysis.D: Schedule III, IV, and V prescriptions are not categorically required to be dispensed in a single transaction.
choice_analysis.E: Each partial filling must be recorded in the same manner as a refilling; the original face quantity does not eliminate that documentation requirement.

visible.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is fitting out a new prescription area. It proposes a dorm-style refrigerator with a small freezer compartment inside the refrigerator space for the few frozen products it stocks, with a continuous temperature logger fitted. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacy may not use an appliance with a freezer compartment inside the refrigerator space.
A freezer unit must be frost-free with an automatic defrost cycle unless the Board approves otherwise.
A continuous logger showing in-range temperatures makes the appliance acceptable.
The pharmacy's procedures must include a response protocol for any out-of-range temperature.
A combination refrigerator/freezer unit would not be permitted either.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.22(2) permits a combination refrigerator/freezer, a standalone refrigerator or a standalone freezer, requires freezer units to be frost-free with an automatic defrost cycle unless the Board otherwise approves, and states that a pharmacy may not use an appliance containing a freezer compartment within the refrigerator space, such as a dorm-style refrigerator. 247 CMR 9.22(1) requires policies including a protocol to respond to any out of range temperature and an assessment of the integrity of the medication.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: the dorm-style appliance is named in the prohibition.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: frost-free with automatic defrost, unless otherwise approved by the Board.
choice_analysis.C: Monitoring is a separate duty; it does not make a prohibited appliance permissible.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: the response protocol is part of the required policies.
choice_analysis.E: A combination refrigerator/freezer is one of the three permitted configurations.

related_facts: Temperatures are measured and maintained in accordance with Board guidance
explanation.mpje_trap: Good monitoring makes the appliance feel defensible. The regulation prohibits the appliance itself, so the quality of the logging never comes into it.

visible.stem: A pharmacy refrigerator is found at 68°F after an overnight equipment failure. Several unopened insulin glargine cartons were stored there, and the pharmacy cannot yet determine how long the temperature was outside the labeled storage range. What should the pharmacist do with those cartons before dispensing?

choices.text: Dispense them normally because unopened prescription stock cannot be adulterated until it reaches a patient.
Relabel each carton with the observed temperature and dispense if the patient accepts the excursion.
Segregate the cartons from saleable stock and resolve product integrity under the labeling/manufacturer information before dispensing.
Return the cartons to refrigeration for one hour; restoring temperature automatically restores legal saleability.
Convert the cartons to patient-return inventory and use the ordinary returned-drug resale rule.

explanation.core_reasoning: The pharmacy must not dispense stock whose storage excursion leaves strength, purity, or quality unresolved. Segregation and product-specific assessment come before any decision to return the stock to saleable inventory.

choice_analysis.A: Pharmacy-owned stock can become unsuitable or adulterated before dispensing when storage conditions compromise quality.
choice_analysis.B: Patient consent does not establish the product's strength, quality, or storage integrity.

visible.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is appropriately licensed for a proposed compounding activity and plans to compound a drug that is hazardous under the applicable standards. Which principles should the pharmacist apply? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Continue to follow the sterile or non-sterile compounding requirements applicable to the preparation.
Apply the current hazardous-drug handling requirements that govern the hazardous ingredient and compounding process.
Treat hazardous-drug status as replacing all other compounding requirements.
Ignore hazardous-drug controls if the prescription is patient-specific.
Use the fact that the pharmacy has a compounding license as proof that no additional hazardous-drug operational controls apply.

Remove the ordinary prescription label and use only the word 'sterile' on the container.
Correct the container to identify the sterile compounded preparation and include the required pharmacist-contact information before outpatient dispensing.
Dispense it unchanged if the patient has previously received another compounded medication from the pharmacy.
Treat the missing information only as a continuing-education issue for the compounding pharmacist.

choice_analysis.B: The additional compounded-product information supplements rather than replaces ordinary applicable labeling duties.

visible.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist and a physician working in the same clinic each point to M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 9 as their authority to hold and give a controlled substance. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The section authorises possession of what is reasonably required for patient treatment.
It authorises administration, or causing administration under direction by a nurse.
The pharmacist appears in the section on the same footing as the physician.
The pharmacist appears only as limited by other named provisions.
Registration under section 7 is unnecessary where the practitioner acts in good faith.

explanation.core_reasoning: Section 9(a) allows the listed practitioners, and a pharmacist AS LIMITED BY s. 7(g) and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 24B1/2, when registered under s. 7 and acting in good faith in the course of a professional practice, to possess controlled substances as may reasonably be required for patient treatment and to administer them or cause them to be administered under direction by a nurse.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: the possession limb is measured by what treatment reasonably requires.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: both administering and causing administration are covered.
choice_analysis.C: The pharmacist alone on the list carries an as-limited qualifier.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: s. 7(g) and c. 112, s. 24B1/2 limit the pharmacist's place on the list.
choice_analysis.E: Good faith is a further condition, not a substitute for registration under s. 7.

related_facts: The good-faith and professional-practice conditions apply to everyone on the list
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates read a long list of professionals as conferring identical authority on each of them.

choices.text: A long-acting injectable antipsychotic such as paliperidone palmitate is eligible.
Testosterone for gender-affirming care is eligible, in any of its salts.
Cabotegravir for prevention of HIV is eligible for administration.
Any long-acting injectable is eligible, since the list gives examples of the class.
The pharmacist is not obliged to administer an eligible medication on request.

choice_analysis.B: Correct: testosterone, all salts, for gender-affirming care.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: named among the HIV prevention medications.
choice_analysis.D: The list is closed, not illustrative of a wider class.

visible.stem: During a shelf audit, a Massachusetts pharmacist finds two naloxone nasal-spray cartons mixed together: one is an FDA-labeled OTC package with Drug Facts, while the other is prescription-labeled and states that federal law prohibits dispensing without a prescription. Both contain naloxone. What is the most appropriate correction?

choices.text: Move both cartons to prescription inventory because Massachusetts treats every naloxone product as prescription-only once it enters a pharmacy.

Keep the OTC-labeled carton available for ordinary retail sale, but return the prescription-labeled carton to prescription inventory for dispensing only through lawful prescription or standing-order authority.
Treat both cartons as OTC when their active ingredient and strength match because the FDA nonprescription status attaches to naloxone itself rather than to the labeled product.
Treat the OTC-labeled carton as prescription-only whenever a customer wants insurance billed because the payment method changes the product's legal classification.
Allow the prescription-labeled carton to be sold from the shelf without an order whenever the purchaser says the naloxone is for a person at risk of overdose.

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts DCP distinguishes FDA-labeled OTC naloxone from prescription naloxone by the product's approved packaging. OTC naloxone may be handled as an OTC retail product, while prescription-labeled naloxone remains subject to the prescription/standing-order dispensing pathway.

choice_analysis.A: Current Massachusetts guidance expressly recognizes FDA-labeled OTC naloxone as a separate nonprescription product category.
choice_analysis.B: The packaging identifies two legally distinct product pathways: ordinary OTC retail sale for the OTC package and prescription or standing-order dispensing for the prescription-labeled package.
choice_analysis.C: OTC status does not automatically convert every naloxone product; Massachusetts DCP directs users to distinguish the products by their FDA-approved packaging.
choice_analysis.D: Insurance billing can affect how a transaction is processed, but it does not transform an FDA-labeled OTC package into a prescription-only product.
choice_analysis.E: Broad naloxone access does not erase the order requirement for a package that remains prescription-labeled; that product requires lawful prescription or standing-order authority.

visible.stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy holds only a standard pharmacy license. Its manager proposes to prepare a complex non-sterile product that requires specialized facilities and training. A commercially available product could meet the patient's clinical needs, but the compounded product would cost less. The prescriber identifies no difference other than price. Which conclusion is most accurate?

The pharmacy needs the complex non-sterile compounding license, but lower price alone establishes a significant clinical difference.
Patient-specific preparation removes the specialty-license requirement, although price alone is not a significant clinical difference.

The proposal cannot proceed as described because the complex activity requires the appropriate specialty license and price alone is not a significant clinical difference.

explanation.mpje_trap: Pre-approval of refill calls is not approval to accept a therapy change discovered during the call.
